chief_complaint: planning pregnancy in 3 months and requires immunisation review
hpi_details: 30F kindergarten teacher presents for preconception counselling, planning to conceive in 3 months. She recently had a pre-marriage checkup which showed she is rubella IgG negative. She is unsure if she ever had chickenpox as a child. She is not currently pregnant; her last menstrual period was 1 week ago and she and her husband are consistently using condoms. She is seeking advice on required vaccinations and general preconception care.
ideas: believes she needs some vaccines before getting pregnant because of her recent blood test results
concerns: worried about catching infections from the children at her kindergarten and how it might affect a future baby
expectations: wants to get all necessary vaccines today and advice on when it is safe to start trying to conceive
pmh: Generally healthy. No chronic illnesses. Pre-marriage checkup showed rubella IgG negative. Unsure about childhood chickenpox history.
medications: None. Not currently taking folic acid.
social_hx: Works as a kindergarten teacher. Married, planning first pregnancy. No smoking, occasional alcohol (plans to stop). Uses condoms for contraception.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Live attenuated vaccines like MMR and varicella are strictly contraindicated if the patient is already pregnant.
Inactivated vaccines like Tdap and influenza are safe during pregnancy and are generally scheduled later in the antenatal period rather than preconception.
common_misconceptions: Assuming Tdap and influenza vaccines should also be given right now, rather than waiting until the patient is actually pregnant.
Advising a 3-month or 6-month wait after live vaccines, whereas current guidelines recommend avoiding pregnancy for just 1 month.
Forgetting to check varicella immunity or administering the vaccine without first confirming lack of immunity.
core_concepts: Women of childbearing age should be screened for immunity to rubella and varicella prior to conception.
Live attenuated vaccines (such as MMR and varicella) are contraindicated during pregnancy due to theoretical risks to the developing fetus.
Pregnancy should be strictly avoided for at least 1 month after receiving live vaccines like MMR and varicella.
Preconception care also includes initiating folic acid supplementation (at least 400 mcg daily) to prevent neural tube defects and reviewing other vaccine statuses (e.g., Hepatitis B).
dangerous_errors: Administering live vaccines (MMR, varicella) to a patient who is already pregnant or not using reliable contraception.
Failing to clearly instruct the patient to strictly avoid pregnancy and continue contraception for 1 month post-vaccination.
Missing the opportunity to start folic acid supplementation well before conception occurs.
diagnostic_clues: Patient is planning pregnancy in 3 months, which safely allows time for live vaccine administration and the required 1-month waiting period.
High-risk occupation as a kindergarten teacher significantly increases exposure to childhood infections, making varicella and rubella immunity crucial.
Confirmed non-pregnant state (LMP 1 week ago, consistent condom use) ensures it is safe to administer live vaccines today.
management_principles: Check varicella serology (IgG) or administer the varicella vaccine if history of chickenpox is completely unknown/negative.
Advise strict continuation of contraception (condoms) to avoid pregnancy for at least 1 month following the administration of live vaccines.
Initiate prenatal vitamins containing at least 400 mcg of folic acid daily starting immediately.
Check Hepatitis B surface antibody/antigen status if not done during the pre-marriage checkup.

source_refs.title: CDC Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women

reference_soap.assessment: 1. Preconception counseling. 2. Rubella non-immune. 3. Varicella immune status unknown. 4. High occupational exposure risk to childhood infections.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: stable and within normal limits. General: well-appearing female in no acute distress. Systemic exam: unremarkable. Lab review: Rubella IgG negative from recent external pre-marriage checkup.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Administer MMR vaccine today. 2. Draw varicella IgG titer today (or administer varicella vaccine if preferred per local protocol, given unknown history). 3. Educate patient to strictly use contraception and avoid pregnancy for 1 month post-vaccination. 4. Start daily folic acid supplementation (400-800 mcg) immediately. 5. Discuss receiving Tdap and influenza vaccines during future pregnancy. 6. Review Hepatitis B status from previous labs.
reference_soap.subjective: 30-year-old female kindergarten teacher planning to conceive in 3 months presents for preconception counseling. She reports a recent pre-marriage checkup showing lack of rubella immunity and is unsure of her childhood chickenpox history. Currently menstruating regularly (LMP 1 week ago) and using condoms. Denies any current medical issues.

learning_objectives: Identify the need for live attenuated vaccines (MMR, varicella) prior to conception in non-immune women.
Counsel patients on the required 1-month interval to avoid pregnancy after receiving live vaccines.
Formulate a comprehensive preconception care plan including folic acid supplementation and review of occupational risks.
Differentiate between vaccines that should be given preconception (live vaccines) versus those recommended during pregnancy (Tdap, influenza).

must_ask.say: When was your last menstrual period, and are you using contraception?
When are you planning to start trying to get pregnant?
Do you know if you ever had chickenpox as a child?
What is your occupation, and are you exposed to children?
Are you taking any supplements like folic acid right now?
Do you have any specific concerns about your health before getting pregnant?

teaching.one_liner: A kindergarten teacher planning pregnancy needs live vaccines like MMR and varicella before conceiving, requiring strict contraception for one month post-vaccination to prevent fetal risk.
red_flags: Unprotected intercourse or possibility of current pregnancy before giving live vaccines.
Lack of folic acid supplementation in early neural tube development.
